profiles.name: Visual-agent / multimodal researcher
profiles.role: Research scientist developing generalist models that perceive and act in visual environments.
profiles.education_technical_background: Authored assumption: PhD-level ML/computer vision/robotics training or equivalent research experience; comfortable with multimodal architectures, temporal reasoning, experimental design and agent rollouts.
interests: Interactive game environments and world consistency
Failure localization, generalization and evidence for repairs
profiles.prior_knowledge: Understands multimodal benchmarks, tool-using agents and perception/action gaps. Knows model demos can hide interaction failures. Has not read these posts and has no privileged knowledge of the source artifacts.
profiles.reading_goal: Find a concrete visual failure and a reproducible check that could improve an evaluation of a generalist visual agent.
continue_signals: An inspectable interaction connects player action to expected behavior and observed failure
Video or a sequence adds evidence beyond the caption
Clear distinction between illustration, matched retest and proposed evaluation
leave_signals: A long project inventory without a research question
A claimed repair supported only by a different encounter
Visual polish substituted for task evidence
profiles.evidence_status: authored archetype; not an interviewed individual or representative population

profiles.name: Research engineer / post-training
profiles.role: Research engineer implementing post-training and evaluation pipelines for generalist multimodal models.
profiles.education_technical_background: Authored assumption: BS/MS in CS/EE or equivalent engineering experience; proficient in Python, distributed experiments, data pipelines and model evaluation; practical familiarity with SFT, preference optimization and RL.
interests: Actionable failure feedback and reliable reward signals
Reproducible harnesses, schemas, tool budgets and verifier behavior
Implementation effort, debugging, retests and valid alternatives
profiles.prior_knowledge: Can interpret rollout logs, reward functions and judge failure modes. Does not assume an evaluation improvement establishes training benefit. Has general GDPval familiarity but no detailed audit knowledge.
profiles.reading_goal: Decide whether one check or feedback pattern is specific enough to try in an existing training/evaluation workflow, and what additional artifacts are needed.
continue_signals: A concrete input/output contract with a failure that can be reproduced
Criterion-level feedback and an explicit retest
Clear setup costs, evidence limits and reusable procedure
leave_signals: No implementation or evidence path behind a claimed check
Rewards translated into training gains without a training experiment
Repeated conceptual framing without a usable next action
profiles.evidence_status: authored archetype; not an interviewed individual or representative population

profiles.name: Evaluation researcher
profiles.role: Research scientist designing agent evaluations and studying whether scores measure intended capabilities.
profiles.education_technical_background: Authored assumption: PhD-level ML/evaluation/statistics training or equivalent research experience; comfortable with construct validity, sampling, uncertainty, judge calibration and adversarial evaluation.
interests: Rubric validity, reward hacking and judge sensitivity
Reference quality, valid alternatives and evidence sufficiency
Comparable model/harness conditions, denominators and selection effects
profiles.prior_knowledge: Understands agent benchmarks, human/model judges and evaluation leakage; has not seen the underlying audits or manuscript. Does not infer professional quality from a deterministic score.
profiles.reading_goal: Decide whether the post supplies a defensible evaluation lesson and enough evidence to test it independently.
continue_signals: Specific failure evidence plus a bounded claim
Clear denominator, selection rule and scorer configuration
Alternatives and counterexamples that could falsify the proposed lesson
leave_signals: Hypothetical probes presented as observed failures
Selected examples turned into population prevalence
Leaderboard differences without compatible conditions or meaningful uncertainty
profiles.evidence_status: authored archetype; not an interviewed individual or representative population

gdpval.reading_goal: Before using a GDPval-style rubric as a reward, identify whether its judge can distinguish substantive task completion from rubric-aware shortcuts, and extract one audit I can run.
gdpval.prior_knowledge: Knows GDPval uses expert comparisons in its original headline evaluation; understands custom rubric/judge audits are a different scoring system. Knows reward hacking and judge reliability; does not know the source submission bundles.
interests: Rubric-aware attacks versus empty and unedited controls
Rendered artifacts versus text-described probes and judge access to diagnostic information
Raw grading provenance, selected rewrites, valid alternatives and missing source evidence
